snippet.title: Metro 2055 - Explore dark subways in this thrilling survival adventure rpg with amazing story!
snippet.description:
In 2049, the world of the game (which was already teetering on the brink of collapse) was changed by a catastrophic event that had the effect of turning the majority of the world's population into horrific creatures (or death) that most resembled zombies. These creatures, dubbed the infected, are extremely aggressive. One by one, they turned some people into their own kind incredibly quickly, while others were simply wiped out. The spread of the creatures, dubbed "the wave", covered the Earth with incredible speed. A person whose body was infected with the mucous tissue of an infected person was changed in an extremely short period of time (from hours to a couple days). The infected transmitted the "infection" by a bite, in which a semblance of saliva, entering the victim's bloodstream, caused irreversible changes in the body.
    The whole human world collapsed, countries ceased to exist. Humanity itself, in its usual form, disappeared. All this happened in a matter of months. People tried to save themselves in different places, but time showed that only those who went deeper underground were able to survive, because the surface was swarming with creatures. Most often, the choice of escape fell on the subways.
    After a while, in the memories and reflections of a handful of survivors, the cause of this event was a large nuclear/biological or some other war between countries (mass stereotypes layered on the horrible reality and confusion of the remnants of people). Now most are certain that there was a war that caused the end of the world, and the surface is poisoned and uninhabitable (but was it a war? Was the surface contaminated?).
    The events of the game take place in 2055, in one of the abandoned metropolitan areas of the United States, 6 years after the end of the world.  The horrors of the surface are increasingly seeping into the subways, along with the hideous infected that the subway residents are increasingly spotting in the stations and tracks.
